text: He reads on his phone: keep replies short, put the answer first, use numbered lists rather than long paragraphs. 53 of 55 sampled sessions were started from a phone.
Use plain, exact words and explain how things work when it matters; no jargon or invented abbreviations. He reads the files and wants to understand the system.
For apps, "done" includes a visual check on a real phone. He notices visual defects quickly, so say what to look at and where.
When a second language is involved, he expects native quality in both Spanish and English, with the same facts in each edition.
He likes one-word triggers he can send from a phone; keep their meaning identical in every project.
He prefers continuous visible progress: many small verified releases he can open, over one large delivery.
His taste is precise, editorial and restrained: clean tables, high contrast, nothing gamified or generic. This applies to documents and reports as well as screens.
His messages are often dictated and fast; read the intent, not the spelling.
He answers questions in chat and rarely fills in questionnaire files. Ask in chat, few questions, each with a default.
He asks for scale and many parallel agents. Deliver throughput within the usage window and say plainly when a cap applies and why.
